Human in the Loop (HITL): AI drives the workflow; the human approves at checkpoints
Human at the Helm: Human directs the workflow; AI executes under direction

Human in the Loop (HITL): At predefined intervention points (approval gates, error correction)
Human at the Helm: Throughout the process, including goal definition and result interpretation

Human in the Loop (HITL): Oversight of individual AI outputs (exception handling)
Human at the Helm: Steering the entire trajectory of the research task

Human in the Loop (HITL): Distributed between system and operator; often ambiguous in practice
Human at the Helm: Retained by the researcher from start to finish

Human in the Loop (HITL): Machine output is assumed usable until flagged
Human at the Helm: Machine output is provisional until the researcher has understood and endorsed it

Human in the Loop (HITL): Can automate reasoning while the human only reacts
Human at the Helm: Preserves human agency; the researcher owns the reasoning and the result

Human in the Loop (HITL): HITL is a system-design pattern common in ML and RL (Zanzotto 2019; Taylor 2023)
Human at the Helm: Extends meaningful human control to research contexts (Jonker et al. 2024; Beck and Burri 2024)

Human in the Loop (HITL): Absent in law; legal discourse requires oversight, not mere presence in a loop (Beck and Burri 2024)
Human at the Helm: Aligns with human oversight and control requirements in AI regulation (Beck and Burri 2024; Monakhov 2026)

Human in the Loop (HITL): Risk of automation bias: the human rubber-stamps machine output
Human at the Helm: Risk reduced by continuous human direction, though the human must stay engaged

Human in the Loop (HITL): Human and AI as separable stages in a pipeline
Human at the Helm: Human and AI as a joint sensemaking process; humans add value AI cannot (Hao et al. 2025)
